messages:
maria_support: FYI ticket #8672 from Acme — they saw their monthly credits go to 0 in the middle of a long streaming inference session, then 429s for ~30s even though the tenant had an automated top-up. Can someone triage? link: https://zendesk.example/8672

kevin_cs: Oof. Customer says stream was uninterrupted for ~20m before first 429. They restarted and saw credits reflected immediately.

maria_support: I grabbed the limited logs from the support stack: 
```
[2026-02-15T09:12:01Z] session id=abc123 read balance=0 -> allowed=false
[2026-02-15T09:12:05Z] refill request tenant=acme amount=5000 status=ok
[2026-02-15T09:12:05Z] refill pubsub: published event refill/tenant/acme
[2026-02-15T09:12:35Z] session id=abc123 read balance=5000 -> allowed=true
```
Looks like ~30s gap between refill and session re-read.

tom_eng: Thanks. Can you paste the gateway cache logs for that session? Curious whether the gateway was still using an older cached balance or if there was a transient negative accounting.

maria_support: Pasted next: 
```
gateway/cache-evict: scheduled eviction key=balance:tenant:acme ttl=60s
gateway/cache-read: key=balance:tenant:acme -> 0 (stale)
```
Note cache TTL here is 60s. Refill published the event but cache eviction was on a timer and didn't happen until TTL expired.

liya_billing: So refill succeeded in the billing service but the gateway kept serving stale balance for active sessions. Does our refill path trigger an immediate cache invalidation?

tom_eng: Currently refill publishes an event; gateways subscribe to events and invalidate on receive. But there’s a window: if a long-lived connection already loaded a local in-memory snapshot (we keep per-connection read state for throughput), we only check the central cache periodically to avoid extra RPCs per token. That optimization is what caused the consistent 429s mid-stream.

kevin_cs: Customer workaround: reconnecting the stream forces a fresh read and reflected the top-up immediately. They did that and were back to normal.

maria_support: Customer asked: is there a permanent fix or a configuration we can recommend? They want to avoid asking their users to reconnect mid-call.

tom_eng: Proposed fixes: 
- short term: reduce per-connection stale window to 5s for tenants with auto-topup enabled (config flag).
- medium term: make refill handler call a gateway control-plane endpoint to immediately invalidate per-connection snapshots (push invalidation).
- long term: change accounting to be eventually-consistent but allow streaming reads to accept refills if there is a pending refill event for the tenant (atomic marker).

liya_billing: Can we also add visibility in Console — show "pending refill" flag and timestamp so SRE/support can see when refill happened vs when gateway applied it? That’ll help investigations.

tom_eng: Agreed. I'll queue a patch: 1) small config change + console visibility in hotfix 2.4.1 (ETA 5 business days), 2) push-invalidation design doc for 2.5.

quota-bot: [alert] tenant=acme refill_latency=32s threshold=30s exceeded -> incident logged INC-4521

maria_support: I'll send the customer the workaround (restart stream) and ETA for the hotfix. Thanks team — leaving notes on the ticket with logs and proposed mitigation.

kevin_cs: Customer reply: "Thanks — we'll do a quick reconnect step for users today. Appreciate the patch ETA." :thumbsup:

maria_support: Closing loop here, will reopen if we see repeat after 2.4.1 deploy.
